subject: Secure dev controls intake — deploy & secret evidence request
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@greenbridge.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intake: secure dev controls for SIG/C AIQ review

Hi Irene,

Greenbridge is kicking off the SIG intake for Redwood and our assessor has a short list of artifacts to validate your secure SDLC controls (code review, CI gating, secrets handling, and deploy/change control). Can you provide the following by next Tuesday (2025-06-17 EOD)?

1) A CSV or spreadsheet showing the CI access matrix (who can run/approve pipelines, who can modify runners/agents) for the last 6 months.
2) Sampling report of merged PRs showing whether pipeline gates passed (static analysis/tests) and who approved the merge (PR metadata).
3) High-level diagram or bullet list of your gated deploy workflow including who can trigger rollback and the escalation path for failed canaries.
4) A short narrative (1-2 paragraphs) describing ephemeral credential handling for CI runners and how long-lived keys are prevented from being used in pipeline steps.

If any of these are sensitive, let me know how you'd prefer to share (redacted attachments, secure Drive link, or an assessor NDA). Happy to clarify scope if needed.

Thanks,
Claire Huang
Senior Assessor, Greenbridge Audit
claire.huang@greenbridge.com

---
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@greenbridge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-14T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: secure dev controls for SIG/C AIQ review

Claire —

Thanks for the clear list. I'll coordinate collection and share a secured folder. Looping in Jordan (Platform Security) and Mina (Release Engineering) — they will pull the CI access matrix and PR sampling.

A couple quick clarifications:
- For (1) do you want raw IAM/SCIM rows or a condensed matrix (user/service account + permissions + last change date)? We can provide both but want to know preferred format.
- For (2) sampling: would you prefer a time-window sample (e.g., last 90 days) or stratified sampling across services (core infra, runtime, control plane)?

We'll aim to share preliminary artifacts via a shared Drive link by Monday morning and attach redacted CSVs for anything with PII. If you prefer encrypted transfer, say the word and we'll use the assessor NDA link.

Irene Choi
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com

Claire / Irene —

Thanks — Jordan here. Per Irene's note, I've pulled the first tranche and uploaded to a restricted Drive folder (link below). Attached to this email are two redacted stubs for immediate review: ci-access-matrix.csv (condensed permissions export) and pr-sampling-report.pdf (20 PRs sampled across infra/runtime/control-plane; includes gate pass/fail and approver).

Summary of what's in the Drive (folder: Redwood-SIG-2025/secure-sdlc):
- ci-access-matrix.csv (redacted usernames; maps role/service-account -> pipeline permissions -> last modified date)
- pr-sampling-report.pdf (20 merged PRs across three services; shows linter/unit-test/canary-check status + approver id)
- deploy-flow.md (short narrative + ascii diagram of gated deploys + rollback authority matrix)
- ephemeral-credentials.md (description of ephemeral runner credential brokering + default TTLs + KMS/HSM integration notes)

Attachment stubs included with this reply:
- ci-access-matrix.csv (CSV, redacted)
- pr-sampling-report.pdf (PDF, redact: developer emails)

Drive link (restricted): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cC_sample_sharedfolder
HubSpot reference: HB-4829 (assessment intake ticket)

Notes/assurances:
- The CI runners use short-lived tokens minted by our internal broker; long-lived keys are kept in our KMS and require a separate approval flow to export. Details are in ephemeral-credentials.md.
- Gated deploys require: (a) passing pipeline gates, (b) two approvers for production rollouts (one from Release Eng, one from Platform Security), and (c) canary monitoring for 45 minutes with automated rollback on defined error thresholds.

If you need raw logs for keystore modifications or a longer PR sample, let us know and we can escalate through our legal/data-share channel.

—Jordan
Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Got everything, thanks — the Drive link and the two attachment stubs arrived cleanly. We'll review the sampling and the deploy-flow narrative this week. Two quick follow-ups:

1) For the CI access matrix, can you add a column for "last approval for access change" if available (we want to see recent governance activity)?
2) For ephemeral credential TTLs, please confirm the default TTL for runner tokens and whether there are any exceptions for maintenance jobs.

If you can add a short note answering those two items in the same Drive folder by EOD Friday (2025-06-20), that would keep us on schedule. If you prefer a quick screen share to walk through the deploy diagram, let's set up 30 minutes next week.

Thanks again — Claire
